mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 5.25% over the prior 8 weeks reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns by 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a 2-week window
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the identified high-rate regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market strengthening that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% while UNRATE decreases by >0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when both indicators move in the predicted direction.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 2% in a month coincides with a surge in consumer demand proxies (HOUST), creating a forward-looking expectation of sustained economic activity that elevates S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month growth > 2% and HOUST month-over-month > 5% in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with the signal (Pearson IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the goods price inflation index (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for three consecutive months reduces the real discount rate applied to equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the deflationary period.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the federal funds rate turns positive (rate hike cycle ends), the immediate 20-day S&P 500 forward return tends to be negative as market anticipates future rate cuts.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) at the confirmed rate-cut onset.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.5% and a sharp rise in labor market friction (PAYEMS) indicates a tight labor market that can cause short-term volatility but often precedes a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market adjusts.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS increases by >10% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when both indicators move as predicted.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged deflation signal from the CPIAUCSL (three consecutive months below 2%) combined with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests a demand-supply imbalance that depresses equity valuations and yields negative 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% for three consecutive months and INDPRO month-over-month < 0.5% in the same period
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant negative relationship with the combined signal (Pearson IC > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of unexpectedly high FEDFUNDS (above 6%) for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return tends to be negative as higher discount rates erode expected future cash flows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the high-rate period.
